purpose: Comprehensive Gospel parable study inventory for the nested Jesus Christ journey; editorial classification, not an official fixed number.
scope: Broad Gospel inventory: 47 narrative or compact parables and judgment pictures, plus 16 selected related comparisons and allegories. The related list is not a claim to enumerate every metaphor in Jesus' teaching.
sourcePolicy: Official scripture is primary. Bible Dictionary and Harmony guide taxonomy and parallels. Notes are original editorial study summaries, not quotations or authoritative new interpretations.

sources.title: Harmony: Perean and Later Judean Ministry

taxonomyNotes: Counts vary when compact comparisons are counted separately. Do not advertise 'the official 47 parables'.
John's shepherd and vine teachings belong in the complete experience but are classified as allegories following the Bible Dictionary; Harmony uses 'parable' for the shepherd.
The Sheep and Goats is a judgment picture included by Harmony among parables.
Each theme is an editorial learning route; preserve Gospel grouping and immediate context.

collections.title: Mercy, Repentance, and the Joy of Returning
collections.introduction: Follow the searches, welcomes, and invitations through which Jesus teaches repentance and mercy.

collections.title: Loving Our Neighbor
collections.introduction: Explore mercy, humility, hospitality, and attention to people in need.

collections.title: Hearing and Living His Word
collections.introduction: Consider the difference between hearing, understanding, speaking, and doing.

collections.title: The Kingdom of God
collections.introduction: Study growth, worth, invitation, and judgment through Jesus' varied comparisons.

collections.title: Faithful Stewardship and the Cost of Discipleship
collections.introduction: Reflect on possessions, responsibility, generosity, and wholehearted commitment.

collections.title: Prayer, Readiness, and His Return
collections.introduction: Keep praying, serve faithfully, and prepare without claiming to know the time.

parables.title: The Wise and Foolish Builders
parables.studyNote: Hearing reaches its purpose in doing Jesus' words. Compare the foundations, not the weather: both houses meet the storm.
parables.setting: Conclusion of Jesus' sermon; Luke first asks why hearers call Him Lord but do not act.
narrativeProgression: Rain and flood test both houses
parables.centralTeaching: Act on His teaching.
parables.interpretiveCaution: Do not imply suffering proves someone's faith was weak.
reflectionPrompts: Which teaching needs action rather than agreement?
What quiet practice could deepen your foundation?

relatedComparisonsAndAllegories.reflectionLabel: Original reflection invitation, not scripture or a promised outcome

editorialSafeguards: Distinguish Jesus' supplied interpretation from later application; do not assign a symbolic meaning to every incidental detail.
Do not merge talents with minas, royal wedding with great supper, budding fig with barren fig, or growing seed with wheat and tares.
Narrative characters are story characters. Do not depict Jesus as literally present inside a parable unless the artwork is explicitly symbolic and approved.
No invented names, biographies, dialogue, exact ages, or unrecorded endings. Illustrations can show plausible surroundings but captions cannot turn those choices into scripture.
Do not use warnings toward particular leaders as condemnation of all Jewish people.
Do not make unjust judges, stewards, or royal violence a complete portrayal of God's character.
Keep reflection optional and compassionate. Do not promise a feeling, recovery timetable, financial result, or guaranteed answer to prayer.
Theme collections may interconnect entries without duplicating ownership of original artwork.
